edges.description: The catalytic subunit is the enzyme; reducing it reduces measured plasma activity.
Histamine and the other granule mediators raise permeability in the superficial dermal microvasculature, which is the wheal.

Angiotensin-converting enzyme is the principal bradykinin-degrading route at physiological concentrations. Inhibiting it removes the compensation that keeps a partial carboxypeptidase N deficiency silent.
edges.source: Angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor and dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitor exposure

edges.description: Raises kinin generation on a background where kinin disposal is already impaired. The intervening step is inferred from oestrogen's known effect on the contact system rather than measured in these patients.

Cold-induced urticaria implies mast-cell activation, but how cold activates it on this genetic background is not established. The claim that the wheal itself is not purely histaminergic does not come from the sentence quoted immediately below - there "H1 antihistamine-resistant" modifies the angioedema, not the urticaria - but from the paper's conclusion across the series, quoted as the second item.
Complete loss of the enzyme, with the resulting anaphylatoxin persistence read out as lethal sensitivity to complement activation.
edges.limitations: The genotype is a complete null and every reported human genotype is hypomorphic, so the model is more severe than the disease. It also demonstrates susceptibility to acute experimental complement activation rather than the spontaneous recurrent attacks that define the human illness.

edges.description: Antihistamine pretreatment converts C5a challenge from uniformly lethal to mostly survivable, placing histamine release downstream of the persisting anaphylatoxin.
edges.limitations: Pharmacological rescue in an acute challenge model; it identifies histamine as a necessary mediator of that lethality without establishing that spontaneous human attacks are histamine-driven to the same degree.

nodes.description: Recurrent, non-pitting deep swelling of subcutaneous and submucosal tissue, predominantly of the face and lips. Attacks are episodic and can be very frequent; the index patient averaged about forty a year over eleven years.

evidence.reference_title: Familial carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The patient with a remarkably low carboxypeptidase N level was a 65-year-old man with an 11-year history of episodic angioedema occurring about 40 times per year.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Patients presented with angioedema and urticaria, mainly on face/lips, but also with abdominal pain or laryngeal symptoms.

nodes.description: Bradykinin is disposed of by more than one enzyme, and carboxypeptidase N is the one that dominates only at high local concentrations. A drug that blocks a parallel route therefore converts a latent partial deficiency into symptomatic angioedema. The reported case is instructive because the deficiency was present both before the drugs were started and a year after they were stopped, while the attacks were not.
nodes.id: Angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor and dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitor exposure

evidence.reference_title: Iatrogenic angioedema associated with ACEi, sitagliptin, and deficiency of 3 enzymes catabolizing bradykinin.
evidence.snippet: ACE, aminopeptidase P and carboxypeptidase N were decreased down to 17%, 42%, 64% of median references values

nodes.description: Aimed at the mast-cell arm, and the evidence cuts both ways. The rationale is the elevated attack-time plasma histamine in the index patient and the antihistamine rescue in the Cpn1-null mouse. Against it, H1 antihistamines at maximal dose failed in the four reported families - which is what the bradykinin arm of the mechanism predicts, since nothing an H1 blocker does touches a B2-receptor ligand. Both results are recorded below.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted disruption of the gene encoding the murine small subunit of carboxypeptidase N (CPN1) causes susceptibility to C5a anaphylatoxin-mediated shock.
evidence.snippet: This C5a-induced mortality was reduced to 20% when CPN1(-/-) mice were treated with an antihistamine before C5a challenge.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: H1 antihistamines, even at the highest dose (20 mg/d desloratadine), failed to relieve symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: symptoms in these families do not respond to H1 antihistamines, and prophylaxis currently recommended for HAE must therefore be adapted.

nodes.description: Variants in CPN1, which encodes the 55-kDa catalytic subunit, reduce the amount or the activity of that subunit. Reported alleles include a frameshift in exon 1 and missense substitutions at conserved residues; probands carry two of them in trans rather than a single homozygous null.

evidence.reference_title: DNA polymorphism and mutations in CPN1, including the genomic basis of carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: In the genomic DNA of the proband, we discovered three CPN1 variants: (1) 385fsInsG, a frameshift mutation in exon 1 due to a single G insertion at nucleotide 385

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: We identified 3 variants of the CPN1 gene encoding the catalytic 55-kDa subunit of CPN: c.533G>A, c.582A>G, and c.734C>T.

nodes.description: Cold is a reported trigger in more than one family, and in one proband it produced frank cold urticaria alongside antihistamine-resistant angioedema. That pairing is the disease in miniature: the wheal looks histaminergic and does not respond to blocking histamine.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: In family D, the proband II.1 presented with cold urticaria and H1 antihistamine–resistant angioedema (up to 20 mg/d cetirizine).

nodes.description: The only complete carboxypeptidase N deficiency that exists in any organism. Every reported human is partially deficient, so this model is the source of the mechanism's causal tests rather than a confirmation of them.

Attacks in the reported families were precipitated by identifiable triggers rather than arising at random: oral contraception, ovarian stimulation for in vitro fertilization, triptorelin, cold, and pressure. The oestrogen-related triggers are the ones with a mechanistic reading, since oestrogen raises factor XII expression and therefore contact-system kinin generation - the same input tranexamic acid reduces.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: with symptoms starting when the proband was under oral contraception

nodes.description: A bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, given on demand for severe episodes in three of the four reported families. It is the one pharmacological treatment here that acts directly on a node in this entry's pathograph: the persisting kinin cannot be cleared, so the receptor it acts on is blocked instead.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Symptoms were relieved by 3 g/d tranexamic acid and 10 mg/d montelukast, and on-demand icatibant in case of severe episodes.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Symptom relief was observed after taking 3 g/d tranexamic acid and on-demand icatibant.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The effectiveness of icatibant on the relief of severe episodes in all 4 families suggests at least partial involvement of bradykinin in the clinical phenotype.

nodes.description: The two arms converge here. B2-receptor signalling on endothelium widens interendothelial junctions in the deeper subcutaneous and submucosal vasculature, and mast-cell mediators do the same in the superficial dermis. Plasma extravasates, and where it does determines whether the lesion is angioedema or a wheal.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Genetic CPN deficiency may contribute to bradykinin and anaphylatoxin accumulation, with synergistic effects in angioedema and urticarial symptoms.

nodes.description: Persisting C5a acts on C5aR on mast cells and basophils and triggers degranulation. In the index patient plasma histamine rose during attacks while serotonin and kinin activity did not, which is the human counterpart of the mouse antihistamine rescue.

evidence.snippet: Plasma histamine was elevated during attacks, but serotonin and kinin activity were not.

nodes.description: A leukotriene receptor antagonist added in family B alongside tranexamic acid. Leukotrienes are mast-cell mediators, so this targets the same arm the H1 antihistamine failed on - which is worth noting rather than assuming the arm is therapeutically dead.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Symptoms were relieved by 3 g/d tranexamic acid and 10 mg/d montelukast, and on-demand icatibant in case of severe episodes.

nodes.description: C3a, C4a and C5a are released normally, but are not converted to their des-Arg forms, so they go on signalling. The mouse data single out C5a: hypersensitivity to complement-driven shock in the Cpn1-null animal is abolished by removing the C5a receptor and not by removing the C3a receptor.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted disruption of the gene encoding the murine small subunit of carboxypeptidase N (CPN1) causes susceptibility to C5a anaphylatoxin-mediated shock.
evidence.snippet: This hypersensitivity was completely resolved in CPN1(-/-)/C5aR(-/-) but not in CPN1(-/-)/C3aR(-/-) mice.

nodes.description: Bradykinin and kallidin keep their C-terminal arginine and therefore keep activating the endothelial B2 receptor instead of being converted to B1-receptor des-Arg ligands. Bradykinin generation is not increased; only its disposal is impaired, and this is what makes the disease a distinct endotype within hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor.

evidence.reference_title: Familial carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Inactivation of C3a and lysyl-bradykinin by his serum was markedly prolonged.

nodes.description: Plasma carboxypeptidase N activity falls to roughly a fifth to a half of the reference median. The enzyme removes a single C-terminal arginine or lysine, so the loss is not of a degradative pathway but of the one step that converts an active mediator into an inactive des-Arg form.

evidence.reference_title: Carboxypeptidase N: a pleiotropic regulator of inflammation.
evidence.snippet: CPN cleaves carboxy-terminal arginines and lysines from peptides found in the bloodstream such as complement anaphylatoxins, kinins, and creatine kinase MM (CK-MM).

evidence.reference_title: Familial carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Inactivation of C3a and lysyl-bradykinin by his serum was markedly prolonged.

nodes.description: The prophylactic backbone across the reported families: 3 g per day, with symptom relief in families A and B. Mechanistically it is a plasmin inhibitor, so it acts on the contact-system input to kinin generation rather than on the catabolic defect this disease actually has - it reduces how much bradykinin is made because the enzyme that should remove it is missing.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Her mother I.2 and her brother II.2 were also symptomatic for angioedema, with symptom relief after taking 3 g/d tranexamic acid.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Symptom relief was observed after taking 3 g/d tranexamic acid and on-demand icatibant.

nodes.description: Superficial wheals accompanying the angioedema, in close to 60 per cent of symptomatic episodes. Their presence is diagnostically awkward, because urticaria is conventionally read as histamine-mediated and angioedema as bradykinin-mediated; here both mediators accumulate at once.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Patients presented with angioedema and urticaria, mainly on face/lips, but also with abdominal pain or laryngeal symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary angioedema with normal C1 inhibitor associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency.
evidence.snippet: An urticarial rash accompanied nearly 60% of symptomatic episodes of angioedema.

nodes.description: Stopping an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor, and a dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitor where one is also being taken, restores the parallel routes of bradykinin disposal. In the one reported case the attacks did not resolve until both were withdrawn, which matters clinically: stopping the angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor alone was not enough.

evidence.reference_title: Iatrogenic angioedema associated with ACEi, sitagliptin, and deficiency of 3 enzymes catabolizing bradykinin.
evidence.snippet: A case is described of Angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi) and sitagliptin induced angioedema, where AO attacks decreased after the withdrawal of lisinopril but resolved only after the withdrawal of sitagliptin, an inhibitor of dipeptylpeptidase IV.
